passage:
Age nine: Akash's aunt rattled off a list. 'Take the blue bag, lock the door, give the key to Mrs Nair, buy bread, and don't forget the milk card.' Akash nodded, then reached the corner shop with only the bread in his head. He came home without the key or the milk card. His aunt sighed, then wrote three short steps on a slip. Next time he did them all.

Age fifteen: Sarika propped her chemistry notes against the lamp, put on a song with lyrics, and set her phone face-up. It buzzed six times in twenty minutes. She read the same page four times and at the end of the hour could not say what a covalent bond was. The next evening she put the phone in another room and swapped to a soft instrumental track. She got through the page in one read.

Age twenty: Bhupen had two exams that week, a shift at the cafe and worries about his father's health. He wrote 12 instead of 21 on a form, left his keys in the fridge and stared at a simple exam question as if it were in another language. A friend said, 'You look wiped.' That night he wrote every task on a sheet, crossed off two he could postpone, and slept a full night.

qa.q: How many times did Sarika's phone buzz in twenty minutes?
What is the shared cause of the slips at nine, fifteen and twenty?
qa.a: Each mind was overloaded. Akash held a long list of instructions and lost most of them, the buzzing phone and lyrics crowded Sarika's chemistry notes, and Bhupen's exams, cafe shift and worries left him foggy and error-prone.

qa.q: What was Bhupen probably feeling when he stared at the simple exam question?
qa.a: Foggy, overwhelmed and worried, as his errors and heavy week show.

qa.q: What change helped Sarika, and why?
qa.a: Moving the phone to another room and swapping lyrics for a soft instrumental track cut the distractions, so the page stuck in one read.

grounding: Mental overload at nine, fifteen and twenty from too many instructions, distractions, and stress, each easing with fewer demands.
